A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoBrain study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the case studies moved from Appendix D to Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original long- and short-video benchmark evaluations, component ablations, training curves, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a manually annotated failure analysis and computational-cost and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The dual sampling agents, iterative inference procedure, data classification, SFT/GRPO training, and behavior-aware rewards are unchanged. Appendix E further documents the existing SigLIP2 encoder without establishing a method modification.

E1.justification: The training datasets and evaluation coverage remain unchanged: four long-video benchmarks, DREAM-1K, and Video-MME Short. The added failure audit and computational measurements introduce no distinct dataset, task, or input environment.

E2.justification: The comparison methods in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. Appendix E evaluates another frame-budget configuration of the existing Qwen3-VL-8B baseline rather than introducing a different comparison method.

E3.justification: New protocols include manual categorization of 70 agent-using failures and LVBench latency evaluation with a 256-frame Qwen3-VL-8B configuration. The timing comparison places VideoBrain and its encoder on one H20 GPU. Previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D–E add targeted failure diagnosis and computational-efficiency analyses. The failure audit distinguishes five error types and illustrates an imprecise retrieval prompt. Existing component ablations, training-curve analyses, and successful case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the same training-reward variability statistics and plotted curves. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are added or revised; the 70-case annotation count concerns evaluation design.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain their scores. New results include failure proportions, such as 54.3% imprecise sampling, and 62.6% first-round answering. Table 7 reports encoder costs of 5 TFLOPs and 3.1 seconds. Table 8 adds the 256-frame baseline's 40.4% accuracy and 90.4-second latency, plus latencies of 30.5 seconds for VideoBrain and 5.1 seconds for the 32-frame baseline.

T1.justification: The frame-selection formulation, GRPO objective, reward equations, and formal validation rules are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs that are subsequently added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and headline findings: dual sampling agents, behavior-aware rewards, 3.5–9.0 percentage-point improvements, 30–40% fewer frames, and short-video generalization.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly identifies inaccurate intervals, imprecise retrieval prompts, and premature stopping as limitations, qualifying the model's difficulty awareness. Appendix E explains that reasoning and multi-turn interaction increase latency relative to the 32-frame baseline while remaining faster than 256-frame inference.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link in the abstract. Appendix E documents shared-GPU inference, concurrent encoder timing, and 0.3 GB of FP32 encoder weights. Existing training resources, model configurations, prompts, and reward implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited research and positioning against earlier sampling and agentic methods remain unchanged. The MLVU publication update and FrameMind bibliographic edits refer to the same works and do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Error Analysis and Computational Cost and Latency appendices, renames the existing case-study appendix from D to F, and adds a generic Impact Statement. Correspondence and publication text are updated; the main scientific narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Three tables are added: failure categories, encoder costs, and end-to-end latency (Tables 6–8). Existing figures and tables retain their content and designs, with limited text reflow and relocation of the case-study material.

improvement.justification: The new failure analysis and latency measurements improve transparency about weaknesses and practical efficiency. Table 8 clarifies that VideoBrain is faster than the 256-frame baseline but slower than the 32-frame baseline, despite using fewer frames. The code-access link also improves reproducibility information. These are useful, targeted additions while the core method and original evidence remain unchanged.
